item.title: Protocol upgrading China-Peru FTA takes effect
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Protocol upgrading China-Peru FTA takes effect BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- The protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement (FTA) took effect on Sunday, according to China's Ministry of Commerce (MOC). China and Peru launched negotiations on the upgrade in November 2018 and signed the protocol on Nov. 14, 2024. The original FTA was signed in 2009 and took effect in 2010. The protocol improves seven existing chapters of the original FTA, covering rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, intellectual property rights, trade in services, temporary entry of business personnel, and investment, the MOC said in an online statement. The protocol also adds five new chapters on standards and conformity assessment cooperation, competition policy, e-commerce, global supply chains, and environment and trade. The two sides also set out future provisions for negotiations on negative lists for trade in services and investment, aimed at further raising openness in these areas, according to the statement. The China-Peru FTA was the first comprehensive free trade agreement China signed with a Latin American country. China is Peru's largest trading partner, largest export market and largest source of imports, while Peru is China's fourth-largest trading partner in Latin America and an important investment destination, said an MOC official. Under the protocol, the new chapter on global supply chains encourages multimodal transport and the development of foreign trade logistics corridors and infrastructure, an innovative arrangement that signals the two countries' commitment to keeping supply chains stable and unimpeded. The chapter on standards and conformity assessment cooperation establishes a dedicated cooperation mechanism and sets out an intended cooperation list, creating a platform for mutual recognition of standards that is expected to reduce trade costs for enterprises. The two sides agreed to launch negotiations on negative lists for trade in services and investment within two years after the protocol takes effect, in a bid to further raise the level of openness in these areas and continue to tap the potential of bilateral trade and investment, the official added. Since the original FTA came into force in 2010, it has played an important role in promoting bilateral economic and trade cooperation. Two-way trade rose from 6.4 billion U.S. dollars in 2009 to 50.4 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, an increase of nearly seven times, official data show. The protocol is expected to help tap further opportunities for bilateral trade and investment cooperation, provide a better business environment for enterprises of both countries and inject new vitality into bilateral economic and trade relations, the MOC said. item.title: China's logistics sees improved performance as industrial upgrades support growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China's logistics sees improved performance as industrial upgrades support growth BEIJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- China's logistics demand maintained steady growth in the first three quarters of the year, supported by industrial upgrading and resilient high-end manufacturing, official data showed Sunday. The total value of national social logistics reached 280 trillion yuan (about 41.7 trillion U.S. dollars) in the January-September period, up 4.9 percent year on year, according to data from the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing. In the first three quarters, the value of industrial goods logistics rose 5.3 percent year on year, contributing 78 percent to the growth of the total. Within this growth, equipment manufacturing and high-tech manufacturing played a prominent leading role, with their shares rising to 37.6 percent and 18.3 percent, respectively, according to the federation. Logistics volumes for new products such as smart wristbands, 3D printing equipment and sensors surged 77.1 percent, 62.5 percent and 16.4 percent year on year, respectively, highlighting an accelerated shift toward new and upgraded industrial logistics demand, the data showed. From January to September, the total cost of social logistics reached 14.8 trillion yuan, up 4.2 percent year on year. The ratio of total social logistics costs to GDP stood at 13.8 percent, down 0.2 percentage points from the same period last year. "The dividends of logistics cost reduction continue to be released to the real economy," said Liu Yuhang, chief engineer of the federation. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, Liu said that with the arrival of the e-commerce peak season and the year-end production rush, logistics demand is expected to be released in a concentrated manner. High-quality logistics development will provide strong support for the recovery of the real economy and the achievement of the full-year economic and social development goals, he said. item.title: China's foreign trade expands in both scale and quality
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China's foreign trade expands in both scale and quality A worker fulfills export orders for spirit levels in a digital production workshop of Zhejiang Shijing Tools Co., Ltd. in east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/Shi Kuanbing) Since the beginning of this year, China's foreign trade has maintained strong growth despite various external shocks and challenges. In September, the value of imports and exports exceeded 5 trillion yuan (about 749.81 billion U.S. dollars) for the first time in a single month. This robust foreign trade performance is evidenced not only by rapid expansion and concurrent improvements in both volume and quality of trade, but also by the vitality and resilience of high-quality development of China's economy. China's foreign trade is growing in both scale and quality. Trade is expanding rapidly. China has become a major trading partner of 169 countries and regions. In the first three quarters of this year, China's total goods imports and exports grew 18.8 percent year on year, with growth accelerating quarter by quarter from 15.3 percent in the first quarter to 18.3 percent in the second and 22.3 percent in the third. China is both a "super seller" and a "super buyer" in the global market. As demand in its vast domestic market continues to be unleashed, imports rose 22.3 percent in the first three quarters. More international tourists are also choosing to travel and shop in China. The composition of traded goods is optimizing. China continues to promote industrial transformation and innovation, accelerating the intelligent, green, and integrated development of manufacturing. This is driving continued improvements in the structure of both exports and imports, with exports becoming increasingly high-tech and green, and imports increasingly innovative and high-quality. In the first three quarters, exports of green products such as electric vehicles, lithium-ion batteries, and wind turbines and their components rose 72.3 percent, 36.4 percent, and 22.4 percent, respectively. Integrated circuit exports surged 99.1 percent. Meanwhile, demand remained strong for intermediate goods, upstream raw materials, and quality products from around the world. Imports of products such as fresh durians from Malaysia, salmon from the Faroe Islands, olive oil from Italy, and perfumes from France all recorded relatively rapid growth. Trade resilience is strengthening. Despite a complex and volatile external environment, China has maintained its position as the world's largest trader in goods. In the first three quarters, its trade with more than 180 countries and regions grew year on year. Imports and exports with its free trade partners increased 30 percent, accounting for more than 70 percent of the increase in total foreign trade. This underscores the results of China's long-term efforts to diversify its trading markets. Wind turbine blades are ready for export at the Lyusi port area of Nantong Port in east China's Jiangsu province. (Photo/Xu Congjun) Behind this strong performance is the continued vitality of industrial innovation and the growing supply of high-quality products in China. Emerging industries in fields such as artificial intelligence, new energy, and new materials continue to post rapid growth, while new growth drivers represented by advanced manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy, and modern services are developing quickly. In the first three quarters, emerging industrial growth drivers contributed more than half of the growth in industrial output. China is implementing an "AI Plus" initiative to promote the digital and intelligent transformation of traditional manufacturing. Over the same period, the value added of the manufacturing of digital products by industrial enterprises above the designated size grew 13.6 percent year on year. Through technological upgrading and digital and intelligent transformation, many Chinese companies have increased the added value of their products and significantly enhanced their overall competitiveness. At the same time, China is accelerating the adoption of green technologies, including energy conservation, carbon reduction, cleaner production and resource recycling. This is spurring the rapid development of green industries such as new energy vehicles, power batteries, and energy-saving and environmental protection equipment, while significantly improving industrial energy efficiency and providing strong support for exports of green products. People shop for imported chocolates at a duty-free mall in Haikou, south China's Hainan province. (Photo/Su Bikun) China's advantages in foreign trade will continue to expand. First, opening-up policies are becoming more favorable and convenient. In recent years, China has signed free trade agreements with more countries and fully implemented zero tariffs for 63 countries. It has deepened economic and trade cooperation with Belt and Road partner countries and introduced special initiatives to facilitate cross-border trade, further removing bottlenecks throughout the foreign trade process. China has also advanced mutual recognition of Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) programs with its trading partners. The scope of its visa-free transit policy has expanded to 57 countries, further facilitating foreign trade and international exchanges. Second, channels for opening up are becoming more efficient and accessible. China is proactively developing high-level platforms for opening up and building diverse, interconnected cross-border logistics networks. It continues to promote regular operations of the China-Europe Railway Express, upgrade opening-up platforms along the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor in western China, and expand multimodal transport services such as air-to-air transfers and air-rail intermodal transport. In the first three quarters, imports and exports transported by air, road and rail all recorded significant growth, rising 60.1 percent, 34.1 percent and 16.4 percent, respectively. Third, the space for opening up is becoming more diverse and expansive. China is steadily diversifying its markets, broadening its network of trading partners. Chinese foreign trade companies are actively adapting to changes in the international market. In response to increasingly personalized consumer demand and a wider variety of use scenarios around the world, they continue to develop new trade formats and offer more customized, user-friendly products and services to global consumers. Products such as portable split air conditioners and compact portable filming devices are gaining popularity. Overall, China's strong foreign trade growth is injecting powerful momentum into global trade and economic growth. Although the international environment remains unpredictable and subject to considerable uncertainty, the world economy continues to demonstrate resilience. Backed by the advantages of its vast domestic market and complete industrial system, and with existing and new policy measures working in synergy, China will continue to unlock the vitality of its foreign trade. (Liu Xiangdong is deputy director and research fellow of the department of research management and information services, China Center for International Economic Exchanges.) item.title: Xi, Peruvian president exchange congratulations on 55th anniversary of ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Xi, Peruvian president exchange congratulations on 55th anniversary of ties BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori on Monday exchanged congratulations on the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Noting that China and Peru are comprehensive strategic partners, Xi said bilateral relations have withstood changes in the international landscape and maintained sound development momentum over the past 55 years. Political mutual trust between the two countries has grown stronger, practical cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results, and friendship between the two peoples has taken deep root, Xi said, noting that China appreciates Peru's consistent adherence to the one-China principle. The protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement took effect on Sunday. It is believed that it will give a strong boost to the upgrade of the China-Peru economic and trade cooperation, and will inject fresh impetus into the development of bilateral relations, Xi said. Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Peru ties, and stands ready to work with President Fujimori to take the 55th anniversary of ties as a new starting point to steer bilateral relations to new heights for the greater benefits of the two peoples. Fujimori, for her part, said that Peru and China have jointly forged a robust bond featuring friendship, mutual respect and cooperation. Bilateral relations have continuously drawn strength from the traditional friendship between the two peoples, and have deepened and expanded within the framework of the comprehensive strategic partnership, she said. Fujimori said the Peruvian side reaffirmed its firm commitment to the one-China principle and stands ready to continue strengthening political dialogue and cooperation with China. item.title: China's marriage registration innovations boost the "sweet economy"
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China's marriage registration innovations boost the "sweet economy" A new couple register for their marriage at a marriage registration site inside an amusement park in Suzhou, east China's Jiangsu Province on April 21, 2025. (Xinhua/He Leijing) * China has allowed couples to complete marriage registration at any qualified civil affairs registry nationwide, making it easier for them to combine registration with travel. * Local governments are improving public services for newlyweds, including premarital health checks, marriage-related legal awareness campaigns and wedding consumption vouchers. * By the end of 2025, China had established 1,330 outdoor sites for certificate presentation and 525 marriage registration sites in parks and other landmark locations. NANJING, Nov. 1 (Xinhua) -- Since China removed the requirement that couples register their marriages in the locality of their household registration, local authorities across the country have been exploring new venues and services to make the process more personalized and memorable. From tourist destinations to football stadiums, music festivals and university campuses, young couples are choosing venues of marriage registration that reflect their interests and love stories. Also contributing to this trend is the growth of China's wedding industry and a range of government measures to support marriage, childbirth and child-rearing. A new couple take part in a group wedding ceremony on boats in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/He Leijing) ROMANTIC MOMENT As a football fan, Wu Jingyu had never imagined that she and her would-be husband would register their marriage outside a football stadium during a match, exchanging vows and receiving their marriage certificate with the roar of the crowd in the background. "It was truly unforgettable. The passion of watching football blended with the joy and romance of getting married," Wu said, recalling the couple's emotional moment outside the home stadium at a recent Jiangsu Football City League match in the city of Wuxi, east China's Jiangsu Province. A photo wall and red ceremonial platform had been set up outside the stadium as a temporary marriage registration venue. Surrounded by cheering fans and family members, couples completed their formalities in a setting far removed from the conventional government service hall. Such arrangements are emerging across China as local authorities seek to meet the preferences of younger couples and give marriage registration a greater sense of occasion. In Nanjing, a city with around 2,500 years of recorded history in Jiangsu, couples interested in traditional culture can wear Han-style wedding robes and phoenix crowns, along with traditional makeup, for their registration ceremony. Other cities have incorporated marriage registration into music festivals, while some universities have organized group wedding ceremonies for alumni returning to their campuses. By the end of 2025, China had established 1,330 outdoor sites for certificate presentation and 525 marriage registration sites in parks and other landmark locations, according to the Ministry of Civil Affairs. "Younger Chinese are exercising greater autonomy in their views on love and marriage," said Zhou Yongbo, a professor at Soochow University in Jiangsu. "They value not only the marriage certificate but also a personalized experience, a sense of ceremony and memories they can cherish." A couple hold a destination wedding in Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, southwest China's Yunnan Province, May 10, 2025. (Xinhua) THE "SWEET ECONOMY" Since May 2025, China has allowed couples to complete marriage registration at any qualified civil affairs registry nationwide, making it easier for them to combine registration with travel. In Lijiang, southwest China's Yunnan Province, a couple exchanged vows in front of the snow-capped Yulong Snow Mountain, framed by a heart-shaped arch of white roses. This province's tourism and cut-flower industries give it natural advantages as a destination-wedding choice, and local scenic areas and wedding companies have moved quickly to build a mature industry. Yang Libin, head of a wedding planning company in Yunnan with over a decade of experience, began focusing on customized destination weddings in 2025. His team uses questionnaires and consultations to learn about couples' stories and preferences before selecting venues and designing ceremonies. "Professional services should improve the couples' experience and make every wedding unique," Yang said. In the first year after their shift of focus, his company organized more than 280 destination weddings. The wedding photography industry is another major part of the "sweet economy." In Lijiang, industry associations have introduced service standards covering makeup, clothing, photo production and after-sales support. Packages costing around 10,000 yuan (about 1,500 U.S. dollars) can include costumes, makeup, private transport and accommodation. By integrating photography, ceremonies and honeymoon travel, Lijiang attracted more than 140,000 couples in 2025, with its wedding industry market exceeding 1.1 billion yuan. In Dali, another popular Yunnan destination, businesses have developed over 30 wedding settings, including lakeside lawns and traditional Bai ethnic courtyards, drawing on the area's Cangshan Mountain and Erhai Lake. Wang Yu, a groom from Hebei Province in north China, and his wife held their ceremony in the morning and took wedding photos near Erhai Lake in the afternoon, while relatives and friends visited nearby attractions. "There were no complicated formalities, and we could combine getting married with traveling. It has been a great experience." A staff member provides marriage counseling service for a new couple at a local civil affairs department in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province on Feb. 14, 2026. (Xinhua/He Leijing) IMPROVED PUBLIC SERVICES While simplifying registration procedures, local governments are also improving services for newlyweds. In Haidian District of Beijing, for example, its maternal and child health care hospital has set up a premarital health center inside the district's marriage registration office. Newlyweds can complete a premarital health check and marriage registration in the same building and on the same day. In Chengdu, capital of southwest China's Sichuan Province, a team from the local court has worked with marriage registration offices on multiple occasions during peak registration periods, giving newlyweds legal handbooks on marriage and family, Civil Code brochures, and briefings on spousal rights, joint property and family dispute resolution. This effort is part of a broader push to embed legal education into the registration process. Many localities have even introduced marriage incentives and wedding consumption vouchers to help newlyweds manage expenses. Also, many provincial-level regions have extended marriage leave, with the longest reaching 30 days. Local governments are seeking to link the development of the "sweet economy" with efforts to create a more supportive environment for marriage, childbirth and child-rearing. In 2025, China introduced 23 measures to support childbirth and child-rearing. Multiple regions have made childbirth-related medical expenses largely or entirely free for families, while Jiangsu has introduced childcare service vouchers. Zhou added that localities are pairing the new registration settings with premarital education and legal consultation, which helps young people understand the rights and obligations of marriage and avoid registering on impulse. "The business of romance is closely connected to people's aspirations for a better life," he said. "As society places greater emphasis on creating a family-friendly environment, preserving that sweetness requires continued innovation in public services." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China steps up efforts to combat climate change
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
China steps up efforts to combat climate change Welding robots assemble new energy heavy trucks on the production line of HANMA Technology Group Co., Ltd. in Ma'anshan, east China's Anhui province. (Photo/Wang Wensheng) China's Ministry of Ecology and Environment recently released an annual report on the country's policies and actions on climate change. According to the report, in 2025, China's carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP were 17.7 percent lower than in 2020. Meanwhile, non-fossil fuels accounted for 21.7 percent of total energy consumption, up from 16 percent in 2020. Installed wind and solar capacity reached 1.84 billion kilowatts. Forest stock volume stood at 20.988 billion cubic meters. New energy vehicles (NEVs) accounted for 50.8 percent of all new vehicle sales. Li Gao, vice minister of ecology and environment, noted that China has achieved significant milestones in addressing climate change and is steadily advancing along a green, low-carbon development path tailored to its national circumstances. "Major progress has been made in decarbonizing the energy and industrial sectors, with several targets outlined in China's 2030 nationally determined contributions (NDCs) already met ahead of schedule," he said. Renewable energy's share of electricity generation continues to climb. Notably, as of July 2025, installed solar capacity surpassed coal-fired power for the first time, establishing it as China's largest electricity source. Furthermore, all incremental electricity demand nationwide was fully met by renewable generation. Industrial transformation is yielding measurable results. The green and low-carbon sector is projected to generate approximately 11 trillion yuan ($1.65 trillion) in output value, supported by over two million enterprises. China now operates the world's most comprehensive clean energy supply chain. From 2021 to 2025, ultra-low-emission retrofits were completed for production capacity totaling 940 million tons of crude steel, 360 million tons of coke, and 470 million tons of cement clinker. Green and low-carbon initiatives in key sectors are making steady progress. In 2025, freight turnover by rail and waterway increased by 20.8 percent and 41.7 percent, respectively, compared with 2020. Ships calling at ports along the Yangtze River Economic Belt used 230 million kilowatt-hours of shore power, four times the 2020 level. Besides, China has continued to promote energy-saving retrofits of existing buildings, while all new buildings are required to meet green building standards. A heating boiler energy-efficiency retrofit is underway at a thermal power plant in Rongcheng, east China's Shandong province, June 11, 2026. (Photo/Li Xinjun) China is also implementing a National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy 2035. Its capabilities in monitoring, early warning, risk assessment, and disaster prevention and mitigation have improved significantly, while climate change adaptation efforts in key sectors and regions have been steadily advanced. The report shows that China has established an integrated meteorological observation system comprising 10 Fengyun meteorological satellites, 842 weather radars, 131 upper-air observation stations, and more than 100,000 ground-based meteorological observation stations, among other facilities. The system can comprehensively monitor and identify 83 percent of hazardous weather events. Initial progress has also been made in developing a territorial spatial framework that incorporates climate change adaptation. To support China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment is accelerating the development of a carbon footprint management system. Li said that as of the end of September this year, China had issued 37 national standards for calculating product carbon footprints, and the national greenhouse gas emission factor database contained 576 emission factors. According to the report, during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021–2025), China's national carbon emissions trading market helped reduce carbon emissions in the thermal power sector by approximately 530 million tons. The market also helped the power generation sector reduce society-wide emissions reduction costs by 56.8 billion yuan. Li said China had established the world's largest carbon emissions trading market. It currently covers around 8.3 billion tons of carbon dioxide emissions, accounting for more than 65 percent of the national total, and cumulative trading of emission quota has exceeded 1 billion tons. China will continue expanding the market's coverage, with the petrochemical, chemical and other industrial sectors to be included by 2027. Photo shows solar panels installed on rooftops of factory buildings in an industrial park in Fangxian county, Shiyan, central China's Hubei province. (Photo/Zhang Qilong) China's voluntary greenhouse gas emissions reduction market is also expanding rapidly. To date, 44 projects have been registered, covering more than 25 million tons of emissions reductions. Trading volume has exceeded 24 million tons, with transaction value approaching 2 billion yuan. The 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) will be held in Antalya, Turkiye, in November this year. Li said China supports making implementation the focus of COP31. It believes the conference should engage in in-depth discussions on longstanding issues, including insufficient emissions reduction efforts and financial support from developed countries, as well as new challenges posed by unilateralism and protectionism, which undermine collective efforts to address climate change. COP31 should help advance the multilateral process by supporting and creating the conditions for all parties, particularly developing countries, to implement their NDCs, and make tangible progress toward achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement.
